title: A connected nilpotent group admits a central series of connected subgroup varieties
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Assume $k$ is perfect: either its characteristic is zero, or its characteristic is a prime $p$ and every element of $k$ is a $p$-th power. Let $G$ be smooth and connected. Suppose there are $s\geq0$ and subgroups $G=H_0\supseteq H_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq H_s=1$ such that for every $0\leq j<s$, every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, $g\in G(R)$ and $h\in H_j(R)$, the commutator $ghg^{-1}h^{-1}$ belongs to $H_{j+1}(R)$. No smoothness or connectedness of the $H_j$ is assumed. Then there are $t\geq0$ and smooth connected subgroups $G=C_0\supseteq C_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq C_t=1$ with the same commutator property: $gcg^{-1}c^{-1}\in C_{j+1}(R)$ for all $j<t$, all $R$, $g\in G(R)$ and $c\in C_j(R)$. The trivial group admits $t=0$.

source.place: Proposition 6.38 and Corollary 6.39, printed pp.133--134; Corollary 6.19 supplies connected subgroup varieties in the descending central series. Centrality is expressed by commutator containment as in Remark 6.35.

proof.text: Set $C_0=G$, which is a smooth connected closed normal subgroup of itself. Recursively, for $0\leq j<s$, apply [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-relative-commutator] with $N=C_j$ and put $C_{j+1}=[G,C_j]$. Its statement supplies a smooth connected normal closed subgroup contained in $C_j$, and $gcg^{-1}c^{-1}\in C_{j+1}(R)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, $g\in G(R)$ and $c\in C_j(R)$. Thus the recursion is defined through $C_s$, and produces a descending sequence with the required commutator property.

source.place: Descending central series before Proposition 6.38, p.133; Remark 6.25(b), p.131.

proof.text: Prove $C_j\subseteq H_j$ by induction for $0\leq j\leq s$. At $j=0$ both subgroups are $G$. Suppose $j<s$ and $C_j\subseteq H_j$. For every $R$, a point $c\in C_j(R)$ lies in $H_j(R)$, so the given central-series hypothesis implies $gcg^{-1}c^{-1}\in H_{j+1}(R)$ for every $g\in G(R)$. Apply the minimality clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-relative-commutator] with $N=C_j$ and $K=H_{j+1}$. It yields $C_{j+1}\subseteq H_{j+1}$. This application requires no smoothness, connectedness or normality of $H_{j+1}$.

source.place: Proposition 6.38, converse proof, p.133: comparison of the descending central series with an arbitrary central series.

proof.text: At $j=s$ the inclusion gives $C_s\subseteq H_s=1$. Every subgroup contains the identity subgroup, so $C_s=1$. Set $t=s$ and take the sequence constructed in step 1; all its terms are smooth connected closed subgroups and it has exactly the required commutator property. If $s=0$, the hypothesis already gives $G=H_0=1$, and the sequence consists of $C_0=G=1$. For a trivial $G$ one can always take $t=0$, irrespective of the length of the supplied sequence.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.38 and Corollary 6.39, printed pp.133–134, using the relative commutator of Definition 6.24 and Remark 6.25(b), p.131.

Every cited place exists and supports what the node or step takes from it. The item's statement, stmt_deps and source are identical to live; live still has the item unsplit and has no repair note, so nothing supersedes this delivery. Step 1 builds C_{j+1}=[G,C_j] by recursion from the new node; the next application needs the output to be normal, smooth and connected, and it is. Step 2 proves C_j⊆H_j by induction: the minimality clause applies to any closed K with K(R) containing all commutators, so it applies to H_{j+1} with no smoothness or normality. This is Milne's converse proof of 6.38. Step 3 (C_s=1, t=s, and the s=0 case) is elementary. The new node is true over any field: the commutator map G×N→N is pointed and its image is closed under inverses, since [g,n]^{-1}=[g^{-1},gng^{-1}]. Then 2.50 gives smoothness, 2.48 connectedness, K=N in 2.46 gives D⊆N, and normality follows from base change to k_s and density of G(k_s). It is strictly smaller than the item and restates none of its clauses. It generalizes lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup (only N=G over an algebraically closed field) and is not a one-line case of lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup, which lacks smoothness and normality; no other node in the DAG duplicates it. Small cases checked: N=1, commutative G, U_3, and infinitesimal K in characteristic p. The perfectness hypothesis is unused but harmless, and the statement was kept.
